# Bird data

We use the Virginia Breeding Bird Alas 2 ([VABBA2](https://vabirdatlas.org/)) data extracted from eBird using the VABBA2 project identifier using the following code applied to raw eBird dataset from Virginia:

```{r eval = F}
library(duckdb)

con <- dbConnect(
  duckdb(),
  dbdir = "processing.duckdb"
)
query <- "
  COPY (
    SELECT
      *
    FROM read_csv_auto('./data/ebd/ebd_US-VA_201801_202212_smp_relJul-2026.txt', types={'PROJECT IDENTIFIERS': 'VARCHAR'})
    WHERE \"PROJECT IDENTIFIERS\" LIKE '%1002%'
  )
  TO './data/ebd/vabba.tsv'
  (FORMAT CSV, HEADER TRUE, DELIMITER '\t')
  "
dbExecute(con, query)
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
remove(con)
remove(query)
```

To get started with the localities and buffers for the study, we will want to get an idea of spatial distribution of VABBA2 observations. Let's pull all unique localities from this study.

```{r}
vabba2 <- read_tsv("./data/ebd/vabba.tsv")

# clean the columns that we will not need

vabba2 <- vabba2 %>%
  filter(CATEGORY == "species", 
         `ALL SPECIES REPORTED` == 1) %>%
  select(`TAXONOMIC ORDER`, `COMMON NAME`, `OBSERVATION COUNT`, `LOCALITY ID`, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE,
         `OBSERVATION DATE`, `TIME OBSERVATIONS STARTED`, `OBSERVER ID`, `SAMPLING EVENT IDENTIFIER`,
         `OBSERVATION TYPE`, `DURATION MINUTES`, `EFFORT DISTANCE KM`, `NUMBER OBSERVERS`) %>%
  rename(taxa_id = `TAXONOMIC ORDER`, taxa = `COMMON NAME`, count = `OBSERVATION COUNT`, 
         locality = `LOCALITY ID`, lat = LATITUDE, long = LONGITUDE,
         date = `OBSERVATION DATE`, time = `TIME OBSERVATIONS STARTED`, observer = `OBSERVER ID`, sei = `SAMPLING EVENT IDENTIFIER`,
         protocol = `OBSERVATION TYPE`, duration = `DURATION MINUTES`, distance = `EFFORT DISTANCE KM`, observers = `NUMBER OBSERVERS`)

# isolate unique locations

locations <- vabba2 %>%
  group_by(locality, lat, long) %>%
  summarise(n = length(unique(sei))) %>%
  ungroup()

# write out

locations %>% write_csv("./data/ebd/locations.csv")
```

VABBA2 sampling coverage was estimated using kernel density estimation ("Heatmap" QGIS 3.34.4 tool) with a 5,000 m radius weighted by number of unique sampling event identifiers via quartic kernel shape and using WGS84/UTM18N CRS (EPSG:32618). Sampling hotspots were identified as pixels with at least 10 observations, and the sampling points were only distributed within such hotspots.

We used the NLCD 2019 to stratify by urbanization level. We assumed 0.9 impervious area for pixels with value 24, 0.65 -- for 23, 0.35 -- for 22, 0.1 -- for 21, and 0 for any other value. Raster resolution was reduced to 1000 m via nearest neighbor. The output raster was then polygonized, dissolved by value, and split into separate vectors. Those vectors were clipped by the extent of the sampling hotspots.

As we stratify sampling points by urbanization, we fit random points within pixels with any amount of impervious area and outside of them. Within reasonably sampled hotspots, we had 39,146 km2 of non-urban area and 6,706 km2 of urban land. Given a radius of 2.5 km, it translates to roughly 19.6 km2 area, which we will round up to 20 km2. Thus, we could fit 6,706/20 = 335 random points within urbanized areas and the same number -- in non-urbanized areas. These points and their 2.5-km non-overlapping buffers will be used as independent sampling points throughout this project, denoted as a `sampleID`.

Now we can download the data on VABBA2 localities intercepting the buffers.

```{r}
locations_assigned <- read_csv("./data/gis/locations_samples.csv")
```

# Climate data

Climatic variables and elevation data were pulled from the [Worldclim](https://www.worldclim.org/data/bioclim.html) dataset. We used QGIS zonal statistics to estimate pixel-mean values for each sampleID for annual mean temperature (band 1), temperature seasonality (band 4), annual precipitation (band 12), precipitation seasonality (band 15), and elevation:

```{r}
sample_climate <- read_csv("./data/gis/buffers_climate.csv")
```

This can also be coupled with percentages of NLCD land cover types, mimicing the approach used by [VABBA2](https://vabirdatlas.org/methods-and-results/analytical-methods/) to model species occurences.

```{r}
sample_land <- read_csv("./data/gis/nlcd_all_classes.csv")
```

# Sampling effort

As a final piece of puzzle, we will add the sampling effort within each sampleID in terms of number of locations sampled, observer-hours, and sampling events.

```{r}
sample_sampling <- vabba2 %>%
  filter(locality %in% locations_assigned$locality) %>%
  distinct(sei, locality, duration, observers) %>%
  left_join(select(locations_assigned, locality, sampleID), by = "locality") %>%
  replace_na(list(duration = 1, observers = 1)) %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  summarise(locs = length(unique(locality)),
            obshrs = sum(duration*observers/60),
            events = length(unique(sei)))
```

# Bird occurrence covariates

Now we combine all of these data into one master dataset.

```{r}
sample_vars <- sample_climate %>%
  mutate(sampleID = fid) %>%
  rename(elev = elev_mean, 
         temp_mean = temp_mean_mean, temp_var = temp_var_mean,
         precip_tot = precip_mean_mean, precip_var = precip_var_mean) %>%
  select(sampleID, lat, long, elev, temp_mean, temp_var, precip_tot, precip_var) %>%
  left_join(
    sample_land %>%
      mutate(sampleID = fid) %>%
      select(sampleID, lc_11_pct, lc_12_pct, lc_21_pct, lc_22_pct, lc_23_pct, 
             lc_24_pct, lc_31_pct, lc_41_pct, lc_42_pct, lc_43_pct, 
             lc_52_pct, lc_71_pct, lc_72_pct, lc_73_pct, lc_74_pct, 
             lc_81_pct, lc_82_pct, lc_90_pct, lc_95_pct, 
             developed_pct, impervious_weighted_pct),
    "sampleID"
  ) %>%
  left_join(sample_sampling, "sampleID")

sample_vars %>% write_csv("SAMPLE_VARS.csv")
```

# Extracting bird occurrence

```{r}
obs <- vabba2 %>%
  inner_join(locations_assigned %>%
               select(locality, sampleID), by = "locality")
```

We will have to ignore all species that occur in less than 100 sampling units (i.e., 5% of 2000 units).

```{r}
obs <- obs %>%
  filter(
    taxa %in% (obs %>%
  group_by(taxa) %>%
  summarise(commonness = length(unique(sampleID))) %>%
  filter(commonness > 100) %>%
  .$taxa)
  ) %>%
  mutate(count = as.numeric(ifelse(count == "X", 1, count)))
```

# Occurrence models

We will fit occurrence and abundance models for each species. Here, we will try a test model for the Northern Flicker. Note that landcover classes 12, 72, 73, 74 were removed due to lack of variation.

```{r}
species <- "Northern Flicker"

dat <- obs %>%
  filter(taxa == species) %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  summarise(occur = 1, abun = sum(count)) %>%
  right_join(sample_vars, by = "sampleID") %>%
  replace_na(list(occur = 0, abun = 0))

fit_occur <- mgcv::gam(
  occur ~
    s(elev, bs = "cr") +
    s(temp_mean, bs = "cr") + s(temp_var, bs = "cr") +
    s(precip_tot, bs = "cr") + s(precip_var, bs = "cr") +
    s(locs, bs = "cr") + s(obshrs, bs = "cr") + s(events, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_11_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_21_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_22_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_23_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_24_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_31_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_41_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_42_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_43_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_52_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_71_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_81_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_82_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_90_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_95_pct, bs = "cr"),
  family = binomial,
  data = dat
)

dat[, paste(species, "occur")] <- predict(fit_occur, 
                                          newdata = dat %>% mutate(locs = 10, obshrs = 10, events = 10), 
                                          type = "response")

dat %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = long, y = lat, color = `Northern Flicker occur`)) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("#fffff0", "#d3ecb6", "#78c8b4", "#3090b2", "#614682"))

fit_abun <- mgcv::gam(
  abun ~
    s(elev, bs = "cr") +
    s(temp_mean, bs = "cr") + s(temp_var, bs = "cr") +
    s(precip_tot, bs = "cr") + s(precip_var, bs = "cr") +
    s(locs, bs = "cr") + s(obshrs, bs = "cr") + s(events, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_11_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_21_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_22_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_23_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_24_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_31_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_41_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_42_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_43_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_52_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_71_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_81_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_82_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_90_pct, bs = "cr") +
    s(lc_95_pct, bs = "cr"),
  family = poisson,
  data = dat
)

dat[, paste(species, "abun")] <- predict(fit_abun, 
                                          newdata = dat %>% mutate(locs = 10, obshrs = 10, events = 10), 
                                          type = "response")

dat %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = long, y = lat, color = `Northern Flicker abun`)) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_color_gradientn(colors = c("#fffff0", "#d3ecb6", "#78c8b4", "#3090b2", "#614682"))
```

Now we can streamline this process for all taxa.

```{r}
taxanames <- unique(obs$taxa_id)

pred_occurrence <- map(
  taxanames,
  function(tx){
    
    cat(paste(tx, "\n"))
    
    dat <- obs %>%
      filter(taxa_id == tx) %>%
      group_by(sampleID) %>%
      summarise(occur = 1, abun = sum(count)) %>%
      right_join(sample_vars, by = "sampleID") %>%
      replace_na(list(occur = 0, abun = 0)) %>%
      arrange(sampleID)
    
    result <- tryCatch(
      {
        fit_occur <- mgcv::bam(
          occur ~
            s(elev, bs = "cr") +
            s(temp_mean, bs = "cr") + s(temp_var, bs = "cr") +
            s(precip_tot, bs = "cr") + s(precip_var, bs = "cr") +
            s(locs, bs = "cr") + s(obshrs, bs = "cr") + s(events, bs = "cr") +
            s(lc_11_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_21_pct, bs = "cr") +
            s(lc_22_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_23_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_24_pct, bs = "cr") +
            s(lc_31_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_41_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_42_pct, bs = "cr") +
            s(lc_43_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_52_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_71_pct, bs = "cr") +
            s(lc_81_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_82_pct, bs = "cr") + s(lc_90_pct, bs = "cr") +
            s(lc_95_pct, bs = "cr"),
          family = binomial,
          data = dat
        )
        
        predict(fit_occur, 
                newdata = dat %>% mutate(locs = 10, obshrs = 10, events = 10), 
                type = "response")
      },
      error = function(e) { 
        return(rep(NA, 2000))
      }
    )
    
    result
    
  }
)
names(pred_occurrence) <- taxanames
pred_occurrence <- pred_occurrence %>% as_tibble()
pred_occurrence <- apply(pred_occurrence, 2, unlist) %>% as_tibble()
pred_occurrence <- pred_occurrence %>%
  mutate(sampleID = 1:2000, .before = `21557`)
```

# NLCD LAND-COVER EXTRACTION - URBANMETRICS
Input:
- virginia_nlcd.tif
- sampleID_buffers.gpkg (layer: sampleid_buffers)
Outputs:
- nlcd_all_classes.csv
- nlcd_buffer_summary.csv
- nlcd_buffers.gpkg
Method 1: Developed land-cover percentage (NLCD 21-24)
Method 2: Class-weighted imperviousness estimate

```{r}

# ---- 1. Environment ----------------------------------------

BASE <- "/RC/group/RC_Walters_Avian/urbanmetrics"



.libPaths(c(
  file.path(BASE, "R_library/4.4"),
  .libPaths()
))



suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(terra)
  library(exactextractr)
})

gis_dir <- file.path(BASE, "data/gis")
out_dir <- file.path(BASE, "results")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
buffer_file <- file.path(gis_dir, "sampleID_buffers.gpkg")
raster_file <- file.path(gis_dir, "virginia_nlcd.tif")



# ---- 2. Read input data -------------------------------------

# Preserve the actual GeoPackage feature ID.

# 'source_fid' avoids conflicts when writing a new GeoPackage.

buf <- st_read(
  buffer_file,
  layer = "sampleid_buffers",
  fid_column_name = "source_fid",
  quiet = TRUE
)



nlcd <- rast(raster_file)


stopifnot(
  nrow(buf) == 2000,
  nlyr(nlcd) == 1,
  all(c("source_fid", "id", "sampleID") %in% names(buf)),
  !anyNA(buf$source_fid),
  !anyDuplicated(buf$source_fid),
  !is.na(st_crs(buf)),
  !any(st_is_empty(buf)),
  all(st_is_valid(buf))
)



# ---- 3. Check raster characteristics -----------------------

# Categorical NLCD values should be integer class codes.
# Do not silently process a fractional imperviousness raster.


# Geographic raster: use coverage_area = TRUE

if (any(!is.finite(res(nlcd))) || any(res(nlcd) <= 0)) {
  stop("Invalid raster resolution.")
}


# NLCD class codes are read directly from the raster cells.
# Do not coerce the entire raster to an in-memory vector.


# ---- 4. Match coordinate systems ----------------------------



if (st_crs(buf) != st_crs(crs(nlcd))) {
  cat("Transforming buffer CRS to raster CRS...\n")
  buf <- st_transform(buf, crs(nlcd))
}



# Record polygon areas in km2.

buf$buffer_area_km2 <- as.numeric(st_area(buf)) / 1e6

print(summary(buf$buffer_area_km2))



# Expected approximate area for a 2.5 km circular buffer:
expected_area <- pi * 2.5^2


# ---- 5. NLCD class definitions ------------------------------



classes <- c(
  11, 12,
  21, 22, 23, 24,
  31,
  41, 42, 43,
  52,
  71, 72, 73, 74,
  81, 82,
  90, 95
)



class_names <- paste0("lc_", classes, "_pct")



# Representative percent imperviousness.

# Non-developed classes are assigned zero in this proxy.

imp_weights <- c(
  "21" = 10,
  "22" = 35,
  "23" = 65,
  "24" = 90
)



# ---- 6. Exact polygon extraction ----------------------------

# For projected rasters with metre units, calculate the area

# represented by each full raster pixel.
# Area weights supplied by exactextractr
# One output vector is returned for every polygon.

# All polygon boundary pixels are coverage-weighted.
summarise_polygon <- function(values, coverage_area) {

  result <- setNames(
    rep(NA_real_, length(classes)),
    class_names
  )



  result <- c(
    result,
    other_class_pct = NA_real_,
    developed_pct = NA_real_,
    impervious_weighted_pct = NA_real_,
    valid_area_km2 = 0
  )



  if (length(values) == 0) {
    return(result)
  }


  valid <- !is.na(values) &
    is.finite(values) &
    is.finite(coverage_area) &
    coverage_area > 0



  if (!any(valid)) {
    return(result)
  }


 v <- as.numeric(values[valid])
 w <- coverage_area[valid]

  total <- sum(w)

  # Proportion for every recognised NLCD category.
  result[class_names] <- vapply(classes, function(k) {
    100 * sum(w[v == k]) / total
  }, numeric(1))



  # Flag unexpected class codes rather than silently losing them.
  result["other_class_pct"] <-
    100 * sum(w[!v %in% classes]) / total



  # Method 1: percentage classified as developed.
  result["developed_pct"] <-
    sum(result[paste0("lc_", 21:24, "_pct")])



  # Method 2: weighted estimate of imperviousness.
  result["impervious_weighted_pct"] <-
    sum(
      result[paste0("lc_", 21:24, "_pct")] *
        unname(imp_weights[as.character(21:24)])
    ) / 100

  # Total valid raster area intersecting the polygon.

  result["valid_area_km2"] <- total / 1e6
  result
}



extracted <- exact_extract(
  nlcd,
  buf,
  fun = function(values, coverage_area) as.data.frame(as.list(summarise_polygon(values, coverage_area))),
  coverage_area = TRUE,
  progress = TRUE
)

extracted <- as.data.frame(extracted)

stopifnot(nrow(extracted) == nrow(buf))


# ---- 7. Create output tables --------------------------------
ids <- st_drop_geometry(buf)[
  , c("source_fid", "id", "sampleID", "buffer_area_km2")
]

names(ids)[names(ids) == "source_fid"] <- "fid"

all_results <- cbind(ids, extracted)

# Approximate fraction of full buffer area with valid NLCD data.
all_results$valid_coverage_pct <- pmin(
  100,
  100 * all_results$valid_area_km2 /
    all_results$buffer_area_km2
)



# Detect implausible coverage rather than masking it.
if (any(all_results$valid_coverage_pct < -0.01 |
        all_results$valid_area_km2 >
          all_results$buffer_area_km2 * 1.01,
        na.rm = TRUE)) {
  warning("Raster coverage and polygon area differ unexpectedly.")
}



# One row for each original fid.
stopifnot(
  nrow(all_results) == 2000,
  !anyDuplicated(all_results$fid)
)



# Detailed results: all classes and QC metrics.
write.csv(
  all_results,
  file.path(out_dir, "nlcd_all_classes.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  na = ""
)



# Compact table for subsequent statistical analysis.
summary_cols <- c(
  "fid",
  "id",
  "sampleID",
  "buffer_area_km2",
  "valid_area_km2",
  "valid_coverage_pct",
  "developed_pct",
  "impervious_weighted_pct",
  paste0("lc_", 21:24, "_pct"),
  "other_class_pct"
)


summary_results <- all_results[, summary_cols]


write.csv(
  summary_results,
  file.path(out_dir, "nlcd_buffer_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  na = ""
)

# ---- 8. Save spatial results --------------------------------
# Keep geometry for later GIS visualisation.
buf_out <- buf

# Remove source_fid to prevent duplicate GeoPackage FID fields.
buf_out$source_fid <- NULL

# Add the extracted attributes by row order; extraction preserves
# the input feature order.
for (nm in names(extracted)) {
  buf_out[[nm]] <- extracted[[nm]]
}

buf_out$valid_coverage_pct <- all_results$valid_coverage_pct



# Preserve original feature ID as an ordinary attribute.

buf_out$buffer_fid <- all_results$fid

st_write(
  buf_out,
  file.path(out_dir, "nlcd_buffers.gpkg"),
  layer = "nlcd_buffers",
  delete_dsn = TRUE,
  quiet = TRUE

)


# Check that class percentages sum to approximately 100%.

class_total <- rowSums(
  all_results[, c(class_names, "other_class_pct")],
  na.rm = FALSE
)

bad_sums <- sum(
  !is.na(class_total) & abs(class_total - 100) > 0.01
)

if (bad_sums > 0) {
  stop("Some NLCD class percentages do not sum to 100%.")
}

```

## sbatch job (NCLD extration)
```{r}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=nlcd_buffers
#SBATCH --partition=main
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=20
#SBATCH --mem=300G
#SBATCH --time=04:00:00
#SBATCH --output=/RC/group/RC_Walters_Avian/urbanmetrics/logs/nlcd_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/RC/group/RC_Walters_Avian/urbanmetrics/logs/nlcd_%j.err
set -euo pipefail
BASE=/RC/group/RC_Walters_Avian/urbanmetrics
module load container_env/0.1
module load R/4.5.1
export R_LIBS_USER="$BASE/R_library/4.4"
export OMP_NUM_THREADS="$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK"
crun.R Rscript "$BASE/scripts/extract_nlcd.R"
```
